And while those outside were pelting those inside,
those inside, with the beams {OCR?} which they let down from the wall, were slaughtering those who approached the wall.
And the sheds covered with hides were of no avail to the sappers of galleries under the wall.
And in three days, thousands died from both sides.
Then, when those outside saw a cracked place in the wall,
they gathered the mangonels against it,
and in two days they breached it.
And the fighting men inside gathered at the breach,
and they multiplied the slain of those outside at it,
so that they were not able to enter.
Then the Romans asked to come out to him,
and he permitted them.
And the bishop and three leaders went out,
and they asked to evacuate the city and leave.
He, however, hardened his heart,
because many of his men had been killed,
and he did not accept.
And when they returned to enter,
one of the leaders, whose name was Boiditzes, turned to al-Mu'tasim and made a pledge regarding his own family, saying:
"I will surrender it easily."
And the king of the Arabs gave him ten thousand darics.
And when he went in, he weakened the resolve of the fighters inside, saying:
"It is enough that you have been killing the Arabs at the breach;
we are captured.
Therefore stay your hands,
lest perhaps they show us mercy."
And in this way the Arabs entered it.
And they captured Aetios the Patrician, and the Eparch, and Boiditzes who surrendered it.
And they laid waste to it in bands upon bands.
And the command went out that they should not kill any more,
but should take the people captive,
and then plunder the city {OCR?}.
And when they had taken captives and plundered,
he set fire to it.
Very numerous in it were the churches and monasteries.
A thousand virgins went into captivity, besides those who were killed.
And when the captives were gathered together, the king saw that the people were very numerous,
and he commanded, and four thousand men from among them were killed.
And when the soldiers began to snatch boys and girls from their mothers,
the wailing of the mothers rose up.
And the king heard and was enraged,
and he arose heated with anger and mounted,
and he with his own hand killed three men holding slaves {OCR?} who met him.
And immediately they assembled the captives,
and part of them he gave to the commanders of the armies,
and part of them to his Turkish slaves,
and part of them they sold to merchants, so that an entire household was sold and children were not separated from their parents.
